entries.answer: Mainland China's Physicians Law Article 9 provides two routes to the practicing-physician examination: a relevant medical bachelor's degree or above with one full year of practice in a medical and health institution under the guidance of a practicing physician; or a relevant medical associate degree, a practicing-assistant-physician certificate, and two full years of practice. Article 64 separately provides transitional arrangements for technical-secondary-school education; specific application must be checked against competent-authority measures. After obtaining the physician qualification by examination, one must register by law, obtain the practice certificate, and practice at the registered location, category, and scope (Articles 12–14). On the US side, BLS OOH explains the medical-school degree, residency training, and state practice licensure separately; state requirements must be checked per the target state. AAAAI's specialty path description: after medical school, three years of internal medicine or pediatrics training with ABIM or ABP examinations, then at least two years of an allergy and immunology fellowship; ABAI specialty certification additionally includes a certification examination. Specialty certification and state practice licensure are two separate sets of requirements and cannot substitute for each other. The US O*NET question asks how much education newly hired applicants need to perform this occupation's work: 53% answered post-doctoral training, 21% a doctorate, and 13% a master's degree; these are respondent answers, not the incumbent education composition or the statutory education threshold for licensure.
